svg.title: The same client-rendered URL, fetched plainly and fetched with a browser
svg.desc: Two columns of equal width for one URL, a client-rendered page. On the left, a plain HTTP GET with no browser returns the shell the server sent: a title element, an empty root division waiting for the script to fill it, and the article sitting below it as inline JSON that nothing has read. The extractor runs on that document and reports 48,522 bytes fetched, 46 bytes kept, six words, by markdownify, and the six words are the title. A cross marks the outcome: nothing a reader would call content. The extractor is not at fault, because there was no article in the document it was handed, and a page that renders nothing is reported as empty rather than dressed up. On the right, a headless browser navigates, waits half a second and reads the document back: the root division now holds an article element with a heading and paragraphs, built by the page's own script. The same extractor reports 50,063 bytes fetched, 1,558 bytes kept, 265 words, by trafilatura, and the words are the article. A tick marks the outcome: the article, for three percent more bytes. The document grew by 1,541 bytes when the script ran, and that is the entire cost of the difference between six words and two hundred and sixty-five.
